body: If the target repository is private, give the worker a dedicated git token with the read and write access needed for branch and pull request workflows. Copy .env.example to .env and set the values you need. ... docker run --rm \ -e CURSOR_API_KEY=your_key \ -e CURSOR_TARGET_REPOSITORY=https://github.com/your-org/your-repo \ -e CURSOR_GIT_TOKEN=your_git_token \ cursor-render-worker

body: May 1, 2026 - import { Agent, CursorAgentError } from "@cursor/sdk"; const agent = await Agent.create({ apiKey: process.env.CURSOR_API_KEY!, name: "Cloud bug fixer", model: { id: "composer-2" }, cloud: { repos: [ { url: "https://github.com/your-org/your-repo", startingRef: "main" }, ], autoCreatePR: true, }, }); console.log(Started cloud agent ${agent.agentId}); repos is an array, but cloud v1 currently supports a single repo per agent. startingRef is the branch or commit the agent starts from.
